chunks: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

The most deserving of the people to show humbleness in private and in public is the bearer of the Quran; and the most deserving of the people in private and in public for salat and fasting is the bearer of the Quran.

Then he called out in his loudest voice: 'O bearer of the Quran! Be humble with it and God will raise you, and do not seek glory through it or God will disgrace you. O bearer of the Quran! Adorn yourself with it for God's sake and God will adorn you with it; and do not adorn yourself with it for the people's sake or God will dishonor you with it.'

Whoever completes the Quran, it is as if prophethood has been placed within his sides — yet no revelation comes to him. And whoever memorizes the Quran, it befits him not to act ignorantly alongside those who act ignorantly toward him, not to become angry toward those who are angry with him, and not to be irritable toward those who are irritable with him — rather, he should pardon, excuse, forgive, and forbear, out of reverence for the Quran.

And whoever has been given the Quran, if he thinks that anyone from among the people has been given something superior to what he has been given, then he has magnified what God has belittled and belittled what God has magnified.

key_terms.التخشع: Al-takhashhu': profound humbleness and submissiveness before God, deeper than mere politeness
key_terms.النبوة: Al-nubuwwa: prophethood — the extraordinary spiritual state attributed metaphorically to Quran completion
key_terms.تواضع: Tawadu': voluntary humility, lowering oneself before God and others
key_terms.حامل القرآن: The bearer/memorizer of the Quran — one who has internalized the Quran in memory and practice
key_terms.يعفو ويصفح ويغفر ويحلم: The four virtues: pardoning, excusing, forgiving, and forbearing — all required of the Quran-bearer

ai.seo_question: What are the responsibilities of one who memorizes and bears the Quran according to a hadith of the Prophet?
ai.summary: The Prophet (SAWW) delivers a solemn exhortation directed at those who bear (memorize) the Quran, establishing them as having the highest responsibility for humbleness, salat, and fasting in both private and public life. Addressing bearers of the Quran directly with a raised voice, he teaches that the Quran must be used for sincerity toward God — as a means of adornment before God — and not for social prestige. The hadith culminates in a warning against undervaluing the Quran: treating it as merely equal to other gifts inverts divine values.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al-Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abdullah, and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Khashaab, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yusuf, from Muaz Bin Sabit, from Amro Bin Jumie, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘

The most rightful of the people with the humbleness in the private and public, is for the bearer (memoriser) of the Quran; and the mort rightful of the people in the private and public with the Salāt and the Fasting, is for the bearer (memoriser) of the Quran’.

Then he<sup>saww</sup> called out in a raised voice: ‘O bearer of the Quran! Be humble with it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Raise you, and do not be bold with it for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Disgrace you. If you adorn with it for the Sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Adorn you with it, and do not adorn with it for the people, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Discredit you with it.

The one who completes the Quran, so it is as if he has inserted the Prophet-hood between his two sides, but there is no Revelation (coming) to him; and the one who collects the Quran, so his Conferment is that he would not be ignorant along with the ones who are ignorant upon it, nor would he be angered regarding the one who would be angered upon him, nor would he be irritable regarding the one who irritates him, but he would be pardoning, and excusing, and forgiving, and forbearing due to the reverence of the Quran.

And the one who has been Given the Quran, if he thinks that anyone else from the people has been Given (anything) more superior than what he has been Given, so he has magnified what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Belittled, and belittled what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Magnified’.
en.sarwar: 5. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf from ibn Thabit from ‘Amr ibn Jami’ from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘

The one expected to be the most humble in private and in public is the carrier of the Holy Quran, the one expected the most to perform prayer and fast in private and in public is the carrier of the Holy Quran.

Then he called out loud, “O carrier of the Holy Quran, beautify with the Holy Quran for the sake of Allah, Allah will beautify you with it, do not beautify with it for the sake of people; Allah for this will cause you to be shunned.

Whoever completes the Holy Quran, it is as if he has saved prophet-hood between his two sides, only divine revelation does not come to him. Whoever collects the Holy Quran has gained handsomely, thus, he toward one who behaves toward him ignorantly, does behave as such, with one who behaves toward him with anger, he does not do as such, and with one who behaves toward him irritably, he does not do so, however, he pardons, ignores, forgives, bears patiently out of respect for the Holy Quran.

If one who has received the Holy Quran thinks that what others have received is better than what he has received, he has given significance to what Allah is has made worthless and has considered as worthless what Allah has given greatness.’”
